newsitem.title: UK: Conoco UK MacCulloch field hit by new delay.
newsitem.headline: Conoco UK MacCulloch field hit by new delay.

text.p: Dupont unit Conoco's MacCulloch oilfield in the North Sea will not begin producing oil until July at the earliest, the company said on Friday.
The field, which lies some 250 km north of Aberdeen in the central North Sea, was originally due on stream in December 1996 but has been hit by a series of weather-related and technical hiccoughs.
Oil from MacCulloch will be transported to Britain's Flotta terminal in the Orkney Islands. Production should peak at 50-60,000 barrels per day (bpd), maintaining that level for 15-18 months.
Oil market talk that the latest delay would force the cancellation of one cargo from the July Flotta loading programme could not be immediately confirmed.
Two cargoes of Flotta crude due to load in June were cancelled because of the delayed start-up.
